# Diagram Design — upstream skill snapshot

Source: https://github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design/blob/7a2e22170ee838e859d8142ba825d83f8b6375e6/skills/diagram-design/SKILL.md

## Working rules carried into Atlas

- Pick the semantic pattern before picking a visual diagram type.
- Draw only when the visual provides more clarity than prose or a table.
- Target one primary question per diagram. Split overloaded diagrams.
- Remove redundant boxes and connections; every edge should mean something.
- Use the shape for node type, not color alone.
- Label relationship direction, cardinality, state branches, and async behavior where they matter.
- Use orthogonal connectors for architecture. Avoid ambiguous diagonal links.
- Distinguish conceptual entity models from physical database schemas.
- A user journey should convey stages and user experience, not disguise a process flow.
- Keep source claims, hypotheses, proposals, and unknowns visibly distinct.
- Use restrained focal accents rather than coloring every node.
- Provide text labels and an explanatory caption; do not rely on color alone.

This is a concise adapted snapshot, not a verbatim copy of the full upstream skill. The exact complete upstream version is available at the immutable source permalink above.
